expectations.text: Stopped before round three with a recorded reason when the remaining hotspots were text speckle, rather than spending the round
expectations.evidence: Three rounds were run: translate/prompts/new-project-dialog-r{1,2,3}.txt, diff/new-project-dialog-r{1,2,3}/report.json, notes.md '## Round 3'. state.json rounds: 3. A recorded stop reason exists ('Round 3 is the ceiling; top hotspot lumDiff 0.029 < 0.04; score moved 0.004 < 0.005') but it is recorded after round three, not before. Note for the author: under the skill's own stopping rule the third round was permitted — round-2 report.json top hotspot 10,12 lumDiff 0.059 (>= 0.04) and the executor sampled luminance and found a fill mismatch (modal bg 26 vs 32, cards 28.5 vs 39.5), not text speckle; round 3 dropped that hotspot to 0.029 and layoutScore 0.9653→0.9692. So the round was justified by the rules, but the assertion as written is literal and fails.

suggestions.reason: Assertion 2 assumes the inspector Details/Tags/History panel is invented by the mockup, but the skill's own SPEC/notes treat it as legitimate chrome of the workbench and both runs built it faithfully; if the eval author knows it is invented (e.g. from the generation prompt), the assertion should state what evidence marks it as invented, otherwise it will fail every honest translation.

Assertion 3 is stated as a literal 'before round three' but the skill's stopping rule (lumDiff < 0.04 AND delta < 0.005) permitted round 3 here (r2 top lumDiff 0.059) and round 3 produced the run's biggest gain; the assertion should be reworded to 'did not spend a round on hotspots the executor had already classified as text speckle' or tie to the numeric rule, otherwise it penalises correct behaviour.
Assertion 4 is only structural; a run that saved prompts and wrote fabricated scores would pass. Add a check that notes.md scores match diff/*/report.json (they do here).
No assertion checks the surface itself: zero colour literals, tokens vendored with .source-sha, or that the render visually matches the mockup — the most important outcome is ungraded.
